title: Stubborn to immovable
core: All five describe a person who will not be moved off a course by outside pressure — advice, argument, offered terms, or begging. What separates them is *which* pressure is failing and how damning the speaker means to be. Read from mild self-will to absolute, permanent hardness: the early members resist persuasion, the late ones resist mercy. Several also detach from opinion entirely and become a fixed hostility or an unstoppable force.
exam_note: The sentence names the pressure that failed — "despite every concession offered" points to intransigent, "no amount of weeping moved him" to obdurate, "ignored every warning and pressed on" to headstrong; wrong answers are the group-mates that resist a different pressure.

words.nuance: The only one that fails by moving rather than by stopping — the problem is no steering, not no brakes. It attaches to the young and spirited (a headstrong daughter, a headstrong lieutenant) and leaves a flicker of admiration the others deny; nobody calls a stain or a peace delegation headstrong.

The plain verdict word: you are still refusing after refusing stopped making sense, possibly to your own cost. Colder and more formal than *stubborn*, and uniquely at home on inanimate things — an obstinate lid, an obstinate cough — because it needs no motive, just failure to yield.

Requires a second party and terms already on the table; it names a stance in a negotiation, not a temperament you carry around. The exasperation belongs to the side trying to close the deal — unions, parties, peace talks — and it says nothing about your heart, only that you will not trade.

The resistance is to pity, not to argument: the pleading is heard, the suffering is visible, and you feel nothing. The speaker is passing moral judgement, not description, and the register runs near-biblical — an obdurate sinner, an obdurate creditor, an obdurate refusal to apologise.

Defined by what cannot buy it off: no apology, concession, or plea registers, because it is a permanent setting rather than a mood you might outlast. It carries hostility with weight (implacable enemies, implacable hatred) and alone extends to impersonal things that simply keep coming — the tide, age, the deadline.
